newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index revisits 6,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index revisits 6,000 level.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average revisited the 6,000-point milestone Monday, as the blue-chip market extended its rally amid signs that the economy is growing at a moderate pace and inflation is in check.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was up 43.23 points at 6,012.61 after jumping 48 points on Friday.
The index was back at 6,000 points for the first time since last Tuesday, when it soared but closed short of the mark.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 11-9 on subdued volume of 186 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose was up 5.78 points at 1,254.05.
Stocks were boosted by Friday's news that the Producer Price Index rose only 0.2 percent in September in a sign that inflation remained tame at the wholesale level.
On Wednesday, the government will report the Consumer Price Index for September. CPI on average is expected to rise 0.3 percent after a 0.1-percent gain in August.
Many investors stayed away as the bond market was closed due to the Columbus Day holiday.
"In a thin market it is not hard to move prices higher or lower," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

"This is the fourth time we have gotten over 6,000 on the Dow, and I suspect that before the day is over we will find ourselves below. The 6,000 level becomes less and less dramatic every time we cross it."
The day was dominated by earnings and expectations of earnings, with Intel Corp. rallying 3/4 to 106-1/8 on expectations of a strong earnings report after the closing bell.
Caterpillar Inc., the world's largest construction and mining equipment maker, rose 1 to 74-1/4 after analysts said they expected the firm's third quarter earnings per share will rise by 30 percent.
Oil stocks also put in a strong showing, a mixed blessing at best.

Texaco Inc. led energy stocks higher as oil prices surged on renewed fighting in Iraqi Kurdistan. Texaco was up 3-1/8 at 101-1/4. Crude oil gained 78 cents at $25.44 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Exxon Corp. was up 1-1/4 at 87-5/8, Chevron Corp. rose 3/4 at 66-1/2 and Mobil Corp. was up 1-3/4 at 118-7/8.
Such strength in the oil sector is a double edged sword, said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"It's not bullish for the overall market," he said. "It could signal commodity inflation, an involuntary tax on the consumer and increased corporate expenses."
